questions.q: Which of the following describes out-crossing?
options: Mating of more closely related individuals within the same breed for 4- 6 generations.
This is the practice of mating of animals within the same breed, but having no common ancestors on either side of their pedigree up to 4-6 generations.
Superior males of one breed are mated with superior females of another breed (of same species).
Male and female animals of two different species are mated.
questions.solution:
Types of Out-breeding:
A. Out-crossing - Breeding between the unrelated animals, which may be of the same breed but having no common ancestors on either side of their pedigree for 4-6 generations.& The offspring of such a mating is known as anout-cross.

B. Cross-breeding - Breeding of animals of different breeds of the same species.
Example:& Hisardale is a new breed of sheep developed in Punjab by crossing Bikaneri ewes and Marino rams.

C. Interspecific hybridization - Breeding of animals of different species.
Example: Mule

questions.solution: Plant callus is a growing mass of unorganized plant parenchyma cells. The culture medium is supplemented with plant growth hormones, such as auxin, cytokinin, and gibberellin, to initiate callus formation or somatic embryogenesis or morphogenesis.

questions.q: Somaclonal variation occurs during
questions.solution:
Somaclonal variation is defined as genetic variation observed among the progeny of plants regenerated from somatic cells cultured in vitro. Although theoretically, all plants regenerated from somatic cells should be clones, a number of observations have indicated that this is not the case. In addition to the basic genetic implications of this phenomenon, the variation has proven useful in breeding programs of various crop plants.

Thus during tissue culture arising from a clone is not always the case, sometimes a variant can be obtained.

2. Micropropagation (b) Plant grown from a hybrid protoplast.
3. Somatic hybrid (c) Producing a large number of plants through tissue culture.
4. Biofortification (d) Capacity to generate.
questions.solution:
Totipotency is the ability of a certain living cells potentially to regenerate whole new individuals.

Micropropagation is a technique of rapidly multiplying plant material to produce many progeny plants. Somatic hybridization is process of fusion of two genetically different somatic cells and formation of a hybrid cell having characteristics of both. Biofortification is a technique of breeding crops to increase their nutritional value

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.chapter: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
questions.q: $Pollen grains of a plant  \left(2n = 28\right) are cultured to get callus by tissue culture. What would be the number of chromosomes in the cells of callus?$
questions.solution:
Pollen grains are formed by meiotic division of microspore mother cell. It contains half of the chromosome of parent cell. Parent plant cell (2n) has 28 chromosomes. Thus, pollen grain will have half the genetic content, that is 'n'. Therefore, it will have 14 chromosome.

Plant tissue culture is a process of growing plant cell in an artificial nutrient medium. The plant part in the media divides to form a mass of cell called callus. The cells leading to callus formation, divide mitotically. Hence, the number of chromosome in the cells of callus formed from pollen grain will have the same genetic content that is 14 chromosome.

questions.solution: Inbreeding refers to the mating of more closely related individuals within the same breed for 4-6 generations. Inbreeding increases homozygosity and can be used to produce pure lines.& However, the continued breeding of closely related animals usually reduces fertility and productivity. This is called inbreeding depression. The cross between the members of the same breed which have no common ancestors for 4 to 6 generation. A single out cross often helps to overcome inbreeding depression.

SCP-single cell proteins are the proteins obtained from the culture of single-celled organisms on an industrial scale as these require minimal nutrients like molasses, sewage, wastewater. These cells can serve as rich sources of food nutrients like proteins. For example, $250g$ of Methylophilus methylotrophus produce 25 x10^{3&}kg& of protein in a day. These microbes also help in reducing environmental pollution.

questions.q:
Which of the following shows the correct sequence of steps involved in breeding a new genetic variety of a crop?

$a.$ Selection and testing of superior recombinants
$b.$ Germplasm collection
$c.$ Cross hybridisation among the selected parents
$d.$ Evaluation and selection
$e.$ Testing, release and commercialization of new cultivars
questions.solution:
For developing a new genetic variety of crop the following breeding processes are followed-

The genetic content of the desired plants is collected and evaluated for its potential. After evaluation, the plant with desired traits is selected. The selected plants are cross-hybridised to gather the gene pools of various germ lines. The progeny with superior variety is selected which undergoes testing for the desired qualities. After testing, the new variety is commercialized and released as new cultivars.

questions.solution: Genetic variations that occur by changing the base sequence is termed mutation. Mutation can lead to formation of new character or trait not observed in the parental organism. Mutations can be induced artificially by using chemicals or radiations and then using the mutated plant with desired character in breeding to develop better variety. Such type of breeding is called mutation breeding. In mung bean, resistance to yellow mosaic virus and powdery mildew were induced by mutations.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.chapter: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
questions.q: Which of the following is not true regarding artificial insemination?
options: Ideal parents are carefully chosen before the female is impregnated.
The semen may be used immediately or can be frozen and used at a later date
The fertilised eggs at 8–32 cells stages, are recovered from the original parent non-surgically and transferred to surrogate mothers.
It helps in overcoming several problems of normal matings.&
questions.solution:
Controlled breeding experiments are carried out using artificial insemination. The semen is collected from the male that is chosen as a parent and injected into the reproductive tract of the selected female by the breeder. The semen may be used immediately or can be frozen and used at a later date. It can also be transported in a frozen form to where the female is housed. In this way desirable matings are carried. Artificial insemination helps us overcome several problems of normal matings.&
In MOET, a cow is administered hormones, with FSH-like activity, to induce follicular maturation and super ovulation – instead of one egg, which they normally yield per cycle, they& produce 6-8 eggs. The animal is either mated with an elite bull or artificially inseminated. The fertilised eggs at 8–32 cells stages, are recovered non-surgically and transferred to surrogate mothers. The genetic mother is available for another round of super ovulation.&

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.chapter: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
questions.q: From which of the following can single-cell protein be obtained?
questions.solution:
One of the alternate sources of proteins for animal and human nutrition is single-cell protein (SCP). Microbes like bacteria, algae or fungi are being grown on an industrial scale as a source of good protein. Microbes like Spirulina can be grown easily on materials like wastewater from potato processing plants (containing starch), straws, molasses, animal manure and even sewage, to be produced in large quantities and can serve as food rich in protein, minerals, fats, carbohydrate and vitamins. Incidentally, such utilisation also reduces environmental pollution.

It has been calculated that a 250kg cow produces 200g of protein per day. In the same period, 250g of a micro-organism like Methylophilus methylotrophus, because of its high rate of biomass production and growth, can be expected to produce 25 tonnes of protein.&
